intro: Tutoring in the tricity means working across Chandigarh, Mohali in Punjab and Panchkula in Haryana, grouped here into four zones. Chandigarh's first-phase Sectors 1 to 30 are mostly plotted houses and builder floors that open onto the street; the second-phase sectors south of Dakshin Marg add housing-board flats, cooperative societies and old Manimajra; Mohali runs in phases and newer sectors out to Aerocity; and Panchkula and Zirakpur mix plotted sectors with gated societies. There is no metro, so tutors travel by two-wheeler, car or bus along the Margs, Madhya Marg and Dakshin Marg above all, and the evening return rush between the three towns is what to plan around.

The board map follows the state line. CBSE, CISCE's ICSE and ISC, and the international programmes are found across the tricity, while on the Mohali side, including Zirakpur, some families study under the Punjab School Education Board, and in Panchkula the Board of School Education Haryana is the state option. Each state board has its own textbooks and papers, so a tutor should teach from that board's prescribed books and past papers rather than assume CBSE material fits. Families can live a few sectors apart and still follow different boards, and a tutor who knows CBSE and one state board helps families who change schools across the line.

Home and online lessons both have a place here. A request from Sector 44 is matched with tutors in that sector first, then the rest of its zone, then elsewhere in the tricity, then online tutors, and the family sees two or three of them with fees shown before a free first demo; switching later costs them nothing. Because sector numbers make homes easy to find, home lessons are simple once the commute works. For Aerocity, outer Zirakpur or a specialist senior paper, an online session alongside home visits is often the practical answer for both sides.

zone_notes.Chandigarh Sectors 1–30: Most homes open straight onto the street, so the sector, block letter and house number, plus which bell to ring for a builder floor, are all you need; there is rarely a gate register. Start evening lessons before the return rush on Madhya Marg and Dakshin Marg, and agree parking near the Sector 22 market, Sadar Bazaar or the Sector 16 stadium.
zone_notes.Chandigarh Sectors 31–56 & Manimajra: Housing-board flats in Sectors 38 to 47 use sub-sector, block and flat numbers that confuse first-time visitors, and the Sector 49 societies have a guard who should know your name before the demo. Manimajra mixes narrow old-town lanes with planned complexes, and Housing Board Chowk is the junction to avoid at its busiest.
zone_notes.Mohali: Mohali's first eleven sectors are called phases, so learn the mapping, such as Phase 7 being Sector 61, and note that the early phases are houses while Phase 10 and Sector 70 add apartment complexes with gate registration. Aerocity has fewer tutors living inside it so far, so tutors from the phases, from Zirakpur or from Chandigarh's southern sectors near Phase 7 can cover it.
zone_notes.Panchkula & Zirakpur: Panchkula Sector 20 and most of Zirakpur are gated societies where you register once at the gate and check visitor parking, while Sectors 8 and 15 are plotted houses and builder floors. Crossing into Chandigarh means Madhya Marg and Housing Board Chowk, and Navratra crowds around Mansa Devi Complex call for earlier or online lessons.

boards: Tricity tutors teach CBSE, ICSE and ISC, the Punjab School Education Board on the Mohali side, the Board of School Education Haryana in Panchkula, and IB or IGCSE. For the two state boards, confirm each year's syllabus and scheme on the board's own website and work from its prescribed books. CBSE sample papers and marking schemes are on the CBSE academic site, and ICSE and ISC regulations on the CISCE site. On your profile, name the boards you actually teach rather than listing all five.
faqs: How do I get tuition requests across Chandigarh, Mohali and Panchkula?

A family sends one request with class, board, subjects, sector or phase and timings. NXTutors offers two or three tutors, taking those in the same sector first, then the same zone, then the rest of the tricity, then online. Listing the sectors and phases you actually reach puts you in front of nearby families.
Can I teach online while living in the tricity?

Yes. You can keep home visits to the sectors near you and teach online for students elsewhere in the tricity or across India. Families wanting a home tutor see local profiles first, while families who choose online tuition can be matched with you directly, which suits specialist ISC, IB or senior science work.
Should I list sectors in all three towns?

Only if you can reach them reliably. A tutor in Sector 35 can serve the southern sectors and Mohali's nearby phases, while one in Panchkula may prefer to stay on the Haryana side and avoid Housing Board Chowk at rush hour. Fewer, accurate sectors match you with families who will keep the lesson time.
How does NXTutors check who I am?

Tutors who join go through an ID check. You confirm your phone or email with a one-time code and upload a government photo ID, which the team reviews before your profile goes live, and real tutors who pass display a Verified badge. It covers identity, not your background; /how-we-verify-tutors explains the steps.
